To start every time you call the surgery they keep you a minimum of 20 - 25 mins on hold.
I called to book an appointment for my 75 year old father, who has a lot of trouble breathing and has a lot of chest pain, confirmed it's not Covid. The most worrying thing is that he's had a swollen and hard calf for the past 5 weeks.
After numerous phone calls he was seen by a doctor and sent to A&E, where they carried out scans to discard a possible thrombosis. Following that, I rang the GP again, ( on hold forever), where they mentioned they would call me back on a friday or a monday, once they would receive the hospital's information.
Not only they did NOT call me, when I phoned this morning and I explained that the most reasonable thing to do was to carry out further tests to understand the reason behind his condition, such as a simple blood test, they said the doctor had to decide whether this was plausible or not, and in order to decide, I had to speak to the doctor.
Only that the earliest available phone call, (forget about a face to face app), is on the 5th of July, being today the 15th of June.
I highlighted the fact that he's extremely unwell but the receptionist was adamant that the earliest and only possible way to contact a doctor was 20 days away.
Considering my father has been unwell and has had a swollen and hard calf for the past 5 weeks for no apparent reason, I have nothing else to feel but an extreme amount of disappointment and hopelessness around this practice, and the doctors who run it.
Will take my father to A & E again, where we are going to have to wait for a number of hours for an elderly person as him to get seen and hoping they can carry out further tests on him.
